item.title: Lab 1.1: MNIST From Pixels to a Neural Network — What Do the Weights Actually Represent?
item.description:
Lab 1.1: What Do the Weights of a Neural Network Actually Represent?

MNIST internals series — the practical companion to the ML notes (softmax & cross-entropy, backprop, training a 2-layer network). This time we stop deriving and start looking.

item.title: Attention: Turning Token Vectors into Context Vectors
item.description:
Attention: Turning Token Vectors into Context Vectors

The embeddings note ended with an honest limitation: a token’s embedding is one fixed row of a learned matrix. The word “bank” gets the same vector in “river bank” and “investment bank”. Everything the model can possibly know about “bank itself” is frozen into that row at training time.

item.title: Softmax and Multiclass Cross-Entropy: Turning Raw Scores Into Probabilities
item.description:
Softmax and Multiclass Cross-Entropy: Turning Raw Scores Into Probabilities

So far, every classification in these notes has been binary — spam or not, XOR’s 0 or 1 — and the output has been single sigmoid feeding binary cross-entropy, whose gradient collapsed to the beautiful $\delta = a - y$ .
